title: How Does an AI Model Work?
audience: Basic science researchers new to AI
objectives: Place current AI capabilities in historical context using the interactive timeline.
Test a personal belief about AI against evidence and read the structured verdict.
Make the four decisions every AI project requires, in order.
Recognise how a preprocessing decision constrains the model choice that follows it.

sections.name: Interactive AI Timeline
sections.purpose: Place today's capabilities in historical context.
sections.how_to_use: Scroll the embedded timeline from Turing in the 1950s through generative models in the 2020s.

sections.name: AI: Fact or Fiction?
sections.purpose: Test a belief about AI against evidence.
sections.how_to_use: Type any statement about AI into the text box and press Enter. The verdict appears with six expandable panels (real-world applications, limitations, research opportunities, AI concepts, datasets, further reading). Requires NAVIGATOR_TOOLKIT_API_KEY; without it the input is disabled and a notice explains why.

sections.name: The AI Project Lifecycle
sections.purpose: Walk a molecular classification project through its four decisions.
sections.how_to_use: One form with four decisions: data source radio, preprocessing multiselect, model radio, validation multiselect. Press 'Review my lifecycle plan' for a single consolidated critique that also flags inconsistencies between stages, such as choosing a scale-sensitive model without selecting feature scaling.

chatbot_guidance: This subsection publishes the Fact-or-Fiction verdict to the AI Guide as live state, so you can refer to the learner's most recent statement and verdict directly.
The lifecycle critique appears only after the form is submitted. If a learner says nothing happened, check whether they pressed the button.
Descriptor or embedding calculation is the one Stage 2 step that is never optional -- raw SMILES strings are text and no model consumes them directly.
Every chart on this page has a 'View chart data as text (accessible alternative)' expander beneath it, holding the same numbers as a table.
